title: Lattice inclusions and rationalization survive scheme pullback
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], continuous coefficient ring sheaves $A_T(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_T(U)=C(|U|,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Locally finite free means free of finite rank on a pro-étale cover, with varying ranks and rank zero allowed. Let $g:Y\to X$ be any scheme morphism. Let $L$ be a locally finite free $E_X$-module, $M$ a locally finite free $A_X$-module, and $i:M\to L$ an $A_X$-linear monomorphism whose induced map $E_X\otimes_{A_X}M\to L$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use canonical coefficient pullback, namely inverse image followed by scalar extension to the coefficient ring on $Y$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then the induced map $g_A^*M\to g_E^*L$ is monic, both modules remain locally finite free, and its scalar-extension adjoint $E_Y\otimes_{A_Y}g_A^*M\to g_E^*L$ is an isomorphism. This adjoint is induced by the pulled-back inclusion itself.

proof.text: For K=WithAbs(E) with the extending spectral norm and A its closed unit ball, the ultrametric inequality makes K and A totally disconnected. Apply the theorem on the actual continuous coefficient adjuncts to obtain cA:g^{-1}A_X≅A_Y and cK:g^{-1}K_X≅K_Y. Naturality of sectionwise postcomposition with A→K and of the inverse-image adjunction gives the compatible ring square.

Let P and Q be the canonical ringed module pullbacks with these coefficient identifications. Let b:Res_X⋙P≅Q⋙Res_Y be the restriction/pullback comparison. Define j=P(i)≫b_L. Canonical module-adjunction units are precisely inverse sections followed by the actual sheafified 1-tensor unit. Naturality of the unit and the unit formula for the mate b prove the required section formula. Adjunction injectivity proves uniqueness. Exactness of P and invertibility of b imply that j is monic.

Apply preservation of finite local freeness by ordinary ringed-site pullback to M and L. The base-change site functor preserves finite limits and covering families. Identify the ordinary module left adjoint with the canonical module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints; transport the finite local bases across that isomorphism.

Let E_X⊣Res_X and E_Y⊣Res_Y be the actual sheafified scalar-extension adjunctions. Form the inverse mate gamma:E_Y P→Q E_X of b. The other mate of b, using the two module pullback adjunctions, is the direct-image restriction comparison and is invertible. The iterated-mate/conjugation identity and invertibility under conjugation show gamma is invertible. For the input scalar-extension isomorphism phi define beta=gamma_M≫Q(phi). It is invertible.

The input section formula says exactly that phi has adjoint i, by the actual sheafified scalar-extension unit formula. The mate unit identity and naturality give adj(beta)=P(adj(phi))≫b_L=j. Evaluate this equality on arbitrary Y-sections, using that same unit formula, to obtain beta(1 tensor m)=j(m). Thus beta is the rationalization adjoint of this specific j.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03DO, finite local bases; Tags 03EL and 03EK, pullback and tensor adjunctions. The canonical restriction/pullback mate implements the parent blueprint restriction-of-lattices argument, with scalar comparison obtained by double mates.
